profile.name: Dhruv Birthal
profile.title: Mechatronics Engineer
aboutMe: I am a Mechatronics Engineer specializing in defense-aerospace structures and precision mechatronics. My work focuses on integrating solid mechanical design with practical control systems to build robust aerial and robotic platforms.

As the Manufacturing Head for Team SAMMPAATI, I oversee the structural and mechanical development of our aerospace projects. Recently, our team designed a hydrogen-electric eVTOL aircraft that secured third place globally in the Vertical Flight Society Design Competition.

I also gained hands-on defense engineering experience interning with the Indian Army 2 Corps Zone Workshop EME, where I handled the mechanical design, simulation, and testing for their military drone systems. Additionally, I co-authored a Springer publication on developing gesture-controlled 3D-printed robotic arms for disaster response. I enjoy tackling complex engineering problems and building practical, end-to-end mechatronic solutions.

projects.title: Gesture Controlled Robotic Arm
projects.summary: Manufacturing and testing of a robotic manipulator mapped to gesture control by fingers.
projects.description:
This mechatronic system translates human finger movements into precise mechanical actions using kinematic mapping and real-time signal processing. The architecture prioritizes the accuracy and repeatability of the full system over standard standalone testing. Developed for disaster relief applications, the system is envisioned to be mounted on an autonomous mobile rover equipped with sensors and cameras, allowing the operator to control it remotely from a safe environment.

VIEW SPRINGER PUBLICATION

projects.title: VFS 42nd SDC 2025
projects.summary: Vertical Flight Society 42nd Student Design Competition entry.
projects.description: As part of the Vertical Flight Society competition, this project involved the complete aerodynamic and structural design of an eVTOL aircraft. The engineering focus centered on balancing the thrust requirements for vertical lift with the aerodynamic efficiency needed for sustained high-speed forward flight, for which I conducted comprehensive structural and vibrational analyses.

projects.title: Space Debris Mitigation
projects.summary: Research and development concerning orbital debris tracking and capture mechanics.
projects.description: This R&D initiative explores the mechanical and kinetic challenges of capturing uncontrolled orbital debris. The project involves theoretical modeling of impact forces, material stress during capture, and the conceptual design of low-mass, high-strength containment mechanisms.

projects.title: Rudra V1
projects.summary: First manufacturing iteration of the Rudra platform.
projects.description: Rudra V1 represents the initial transition from CAD to physical reality. Key engineering efforts focused on validating the structural layout through rapid prototyping and assessing the manufacturability of the core load-bearing components. This drone is designed to deliver five independent packages to different locations, utilizing a custom delivery mechanism that integrates a rack-and-pinion system to actuate the package holding plates.

projects.title: Vajra V1
projects.summary: Heavy-lift multirotor engineered for automated munition deployment.
projects.description: Designed for rapid deployment and fabrication, this heavy-lift multirotor integrates carbon-polymer composites to maximize payload capacity. Extensive finite element analysis was conducted on the airframe to ensure it could withstand the severe vibrations and dynamic stress loads induced during automated munition release sequences. This platform is part of a multi-drone network known as Project Hailing Swarm Drones.

projects.title: Pralay V3
projects.summary: Evolution of the Pralay conceptual layout and first physical prototype.
projects.description: Spanning three major conceptual overhauls, the Pralay design evolution highlights an iterative approach to defense architecture. Each version progressively refined the airframe's stiffness-to-weight ratio and optimized the internal volumetric efficiency for modular payloads. This specific iteration serves as the first fully manufacturable model in the system's development.

projects.title: Pralay V4
projects.summary: Iteration 4 manufacturing sequence of the Pralay defense architecture.
projects.description: Building upon previous conceptual iterations, the V4 phase translates the Pralay architecture into highly capable physical, manufacturable components. This stage involved rigorous material selection and the development of custom fixturing to significantly streamline the assembly of the primary chassis. This platform serves as a critical asset within the Project Hailing Swarm Drones system.

projects.title: Passive Release Perching Mechanism
projects.summary: Multi-component weight-actuated payload delivery mechanism using tight geometric tolerances.
projects.description: Engineered specifically for autonomous drone applications, this passive release mechanism utilizes the drone's own mass to actuate the gripper sequence. Strict geometric tolerance optimizations ensure reliable perching without requiring auxiliary electronic actuators, drastically reducing overall vehicle weight and complexity. This mechanism is critical for preserving battery life when the drone needs to maintain a static, elevated vantage point.

projects.title: Parshu V1 & V2
projects.summary: Conceptual architecture and structural layout for the Parshu airframe.
projects.description: The Parshu platform was developed entirely in the conceptual phase to establish base geometric and payload parameters, with its primary function focused heavily on high-endurance flight and sustained aerial surveillance. Iterations V1 and V2 prioritized packaging optimization, avionics placement, and ensuring a highly favorable center of gravity for dynamic flight operations.

projects.title: Rudra V2
projects.summary: Advanced conceptual framework for Rudra iteration 2.
projects.description: Applying the lessons learned from the initial V1 manufacturing prototype, the Rudra V2 conceptual model introduces significant geometric refinements designed to handle a substantial increase in payload capacity. The engineering focus is on reducing part count, streamlining physical assembly, accommodating heavier operational payloads, and increasing the overall survivability of the platform.

projects.title: Nidar 27
projects.summary: Design, manufacturing, and assembly architecture for the Nidar 27 competition.
projects.description: A comprehensive design and assembly pipeline detailing the integration of critical sub-systems for the Nidar 27 competition. The focus of this phase is optimizing component geometry for rapid additive manufacturing without sacrificing structural integrity, ensuring the platform is fast and highly efficient to construct on an assembly line.
